Alex Kim: hey @people-ops :wave: quick question — I was a contractor from Jan 10 and converted to full-time on Jan 25. I missed the original enrollment cutoff. When will my 401(k) and HSA elections actually take effect? Is employer match prorated for the partial pay period? Can anything be applied retroactively to the contractor pay?
Maria Gonzales: congrats on the conversion! short answer: benefits effective date is based on FT start date and the plan's effective rules. our standard is: benefits become effective the first of the month after 30 days of FT service. since your FT start was 2024-01-25, that puts benefits effective 2024-03-01. employer match applies only to eligible wages paid after your benefits effective date (so not contractor earnings).
Maria Gonzales: if you submitted enrollment before the payroll cutoff for the pay period that includes the effective date, your pre-tax payroll deductions can start on the first paycheck after 3/1. if you need match for the first partial pay period we can check with payroll for a one-off correction, but we don't retroactively match contractor earnings.
Alex Kim: ok thanks — what is the payroll cutoff? i have a paycheck that posts 2/28 vs 3/15 and want to know if my HSA deduction can land on 2/28.
Maria Gonzales: payroll cuts off at 23:59 PT on the 5th and 20th of each month. included here for clarity:
```
Payroll cutoff windows (PT):
- 5th 23:59 => affects pay dates on/after 15th
- 20th 23:59 => affects pay dates on/after end-of-month
```
Maria Gonzales: so to get contributions on the pay that posts 2/28 we'd have needed enrollment submitted by 23:59 PT on 2/20. since enrollment will be effective 3/1, your first pre-tax HSA and 401(k) deferrals should appear on the next paycheck after 3/1 (likely the 3/15 pay).
Alex Kim: makes sense. is there any path to request a retroactive employer match for the days i was a contractor? i'm happy to provide invoices/pay records.
Maria Gonzales: short: no, contractor earnings are not eligible for employer match. we can make a limited exception if there was an admin error where you should have been on payroll as a W-2 but were paid as a contractor; in that case open a ticket with payroll + benefits with supporting docs and we can evaluate. otherwise match only applies to eligible wages paid as an employee after benefits effective date.
Charlie Patel: FWIW i converted mid-month last quarter — enrolled the same day and my 401k contributions started on the first paycheck after my benefits effective date. payroll was pretty fast with the change once benefits processed.
Alex Kim: got it, thanks both. one more: any forms i should fill for the conversion-specific flow?
Maria Gonzales: yes — please fill out the "Conversion Enrollment" benefits form here: https://redwood/hr/forms/conversion-enrollment and pick your 401(k) deferral % + HSA election. deadline to guarantee 3/1 coverage is 2024-02-28 23:59 PT. after that we can still enroll you but your first deduction may be delayed to the following cycle. if you want, i can flag payroll after you submit to double-check.
Alex Kim: submitting now. thanks! :thumbsup:
Benefits Bot: Enrollment received for Alex Kim. Reference ID: ENR-20240215-789. A member of People Ops will follow up if anything else is needed.
